title: Amazon signage: set up a device and assign your kiosk app
summary: Enrol an Amazon signage device in your device management console, add the kiosk app and set it to auto-launch at start-up — the Amazon counterpart to the ChromeOS/Google CDM walkthrough.
bodyMd:
Amazon signage devices (Fire TV / Amazon Signage Stick hardware set up for kiosk use) can run the Personalisation Hub kiosk player the same way a ChromeOS display does — enrolled in a device management console, with the kiosk app set to auto-launch. This article mirrors the ChromeOS walkthrough (ChromeOS: set up a new organisational unit in Google CDM and ChromeOS: register a Chromebox with Google CDM and assign your kiosk app) for the Amazon device flow. Allow about 20 minutes per device.

Before you begin

  • The Amazon signage device powered on and connected to the internet.
  • Administrator access to your organisation's Amazon device management console.
  • An organisational grouping for your displays, matching the environment/display-type structure used for ChromeOS displays — see ChromeOS: set up a new organisational unit in Google CDM for the recommended layout.
  • The kiosk player's app URL and companion extension details for your organisation.

Set up a device group

  1. Sign in to your Amazon device management console.
  2. Create a device group (organisational-unit equivalent) for the project, with a child group per environment and per display type, mirroring the ChromeOS OU structure.
  3. Define the device settings for the group, including kiosk/single-app mode.

Enrol the device

  1. Turn on the Amazon signage device and connect it to the internet.
  2. Follow the on-screen prompts to enrol it into your organisation's device management console and assign it to the device group you created.

Add the kiosk app

As with ChromeOS, the kiosk player runs as a web app rather than a store-listed app, so it is added by URL rather than by searching an app store — the same detail that is easy to miss on the ChromeOS setup.

  1. In the device group's settings, add the kiosk player by its app URL.
  2. Add the companion extension/configuration the kiosk player needs, using the JSON configuration for your organisation, the same as the ChromeOS companion-extension step.
  3. Set the kiosk app to auto-launch on startup and save.

Verify it worked

Restart the device. It starts straight into the kiosk app. When the app connects to your platform domain, it shows a Register this display screen with a registration code — continue with Register a new display or device.

Troubleshooting

The kiosk app does not launch after restart

Cause. The device was offline when you saved the settings, or it sits in a different device group from the one you configured.

Fix. Connect the device to the internet and restart it. Confirm which device group the device belongs to in your Amazon device management console.
